format.tagged_pdf_tooltip:
A copy of the source PDF with structure tags added: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables.

The pages look the same, but screen readers and other programs can now read the document in the right order.
format.pdf_tooltip:
A copy of the source PDF with everything the converter recognised drawn over the pages: table cells with their borders, text blocks, headings.

It holds no text of its own — it shows why a table came out wrong. Saved as name_annotated.pdf; it hardly affects the speed.
images.label: Images:
images.tooltip:
Separate files — PNG or JPEG images next to the document, linked from the text.

In the document — the images go inside the .md file as Base64: one self-contained file, but several times bigger.

Don't save — text and tables only; the fastest choice.
images.hint: Extracting images is the heaviest part of the job: every illustration is rendered again. On ordinary documents you won't notice, but datasheets can have dozens of pages of plots, and those can take minutes.
dpi.label: Resolution:
dpi.tooltip:
How sharp the extracted images are. Lower is faster and needs less memory, but the pictures are coarser.

144 is the default; 96 is usually enough for datasheet plots. Matters only when images are saved.
pages.label: Pages:
pages.tooltip:
Which pages to convert, e.g. 1,3,5-7. Empty means all of them.

With datasheets it pays to take the description and the parameter tables (say 1-12) and skip dozens of pages of plots.
timeout.label: Timeout per file:
timeout.tooltip:
How long one file may take. A file that runs over is tried once more without images, and only then marked as not converted; the rest of the batch carries on.

“No limit” lets a file take as long as it needs.
struct.label: Use tags from the PDF
struct.tooltip:
Some PDFs carry tags describing their structure — headings, lists, tables. With this on, the converter follows those tags instead of working the layout out from the page.

More accurate when the tags are good, worse when they are sloppy. PDFs without tags are converted as usual.
sanitize.label: Hide sensitive data
sanitize.tooltip:
Replaces e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, card numbers and web links in the result with placeholders.

Useful before you share the text. The source PDF is not changed.
page_sep.label: Page separators
page_sep.tooltip:
Puts a line such as “---- page 3 ----” between the pages in Markdown, text and HTML, so you can tell which page a passage came from.

Off — the pages run on as one continuous text.
plain_md.label: Plain Markdown tables
plain_md.tooltip:
Writes tables in Markdown's own | pipe | form instead of HTML: about a quarter shorter, a third fewer tokens for a language model. Everything else is done first - MIN, TYP and MAX in their own columns, figure clutter removed.

Markdown cannot merge cells, so a merged cell's other places stay empty; some editors line such tables up less neatly. On by default. Affects Markdown only.
clean_figures.label: Drop figure clutter
clean_figures.tooltip:
Plots, package drawings and flow charts often come out as huge tables of empty cells with scattered tick labels — in a datasheet up to three quarters of the file. This replaces each with one line: a figure was here, its caption and page. Real sentences inside, such as the steps of a flow chart, are kept.

The figure itself is not in the Markdown either way; look at the page in the PDF. Affects Markdown with HTML tables.
reading_order.label: Reading order:
reading_order.tooltip:
The order in which the text blocks of a page are read.

xycut (the default) cuts the page into columns and rows, which suits most documents. Off keeps the order the text is stored in inside the PDF — try it when a page with an unusual layout comes out jumbled.
tables.label: Tables:
tables.tooltip:
How tables are found.

By ruling lines — from the lines drawn between cells; the default.

By clusters — also groups text into cells by its position. Helps with tables that have only some of their lines drawn, which is common in datasheets.
image_format.label: Image format:
image_format.tooltip:
File type of the saved images. PNG keeps plots and diagrams sharp; JPEG makes photos smaller.

Matters only when images are saved.
threads.label: Threads:
threads.tooltip:
How many processor cores work on the pages of one file at the same time. The files themselves are still converted one after another.

1 is the default and the most reliable. More is experimental: the result may differ slightly on some PDFs, and on real datasheets it saved only 5–10% of the time. Ignored in AI mode.
space_ratio.label: Space threshold:
space_ratio.tooltip:
When to put a space between two neighbouring letters: when the gap is wider than this share of the font size.

Lower — words start falling apart; higher — they run together. 0.17 is the default; change it only if words in the result are broken up or glued together.
password.label: PDF password:
password.tooltip:
Needed only for PDFs that ask for a password to open. Used for this run only and never saved.

The eye button shows what you typed.
line_breaks.label: Keep line breaks
line_breaks.tooltip:
Keeps the line breaks exactly as on the page.

Off joins the lines of a paragraph into one — that reads and searches better.
header_footer.label: Include headers and footers
header_footer.tooltip:
Includes running headers and footers: page numbers, the document title, the company name repeated on every page.

Off leaves them out so they don't break up the text.
strikethrough.label: Mark strikethrough text
strikethrough.tooltip: Marks crossed-out text: ~~like this~~ in Markdown, <del> in HTML. Experimental.
hidden_text.label: Drop hidden text
hidden_text.tooltip:
For results that go to an AI. A PDF can carry text the reader never sees — invisible, white on white, microscopic, outside the page, in hidden layers — sometimes with instructions meant for the AI. This drops all of it.

The price: about twice as slow, and thin signs go with it — plus, minus, equals. In formulas and code that changes the meaning: on a Bosch datasheet "var1 + var2" became "var1 var2". Do not use it for documents with formulas or code. Off by default.
hybrid.label: AI mode:
hybrid.tooltip:
Sends the difficult pages — complex tables, scans — to a separate AI server (docling) for better recognition; the rest is converted as usual.

The server is installed and started separately: pip install "opendataloader-pdf[hybrid]", then opendataloader-pdf-hybrid --port 5002. If it doesn't answer, the program tells you before starting.
hybrid_url.label: Server address:
hybrid_url.tooltip: Address of the AI server. Leave it empty for a server on this computer (http://localhost:5002); fill it in only if the server runs elsewhere.
